The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is $P = 2 \cdot (L + W)$, where $L$ is the length and $W$ is the width. We are given that the perimeter is $30$ cm and the length is $9$ cm. We can solve for the width:

$$
\begin{equation*}
30 \text{ cm} = 2 \cdot (9 \text{ cm} + W) \, .
\end{equation*}
$$

Simplifying the equation, we get:

$$
\begin{align*}
15 \text{ cm} & = 9 \text{ cm} + W \\
6 \text{ cm} & = W \, .
\end{align*}
$$

So, the width of the rectangle is $6$ cm.

Now, we can find the area of the rectangle using the formula $A = L \cdot W$:

$$
\begin{equation*}
A = 9 \text{ cm} \cdot 6 \text{ cm} = 54 \text{ cm}^2 \, .
\end{equation*}
$$

Therefore, the area of the rectangle is $\boxed{54 \text{ cm}^2}$.

Answer: $54$
